drawings.description: schéma : $F' \ll F$ sur la première ligne ; sous $F'$, $X' \leq F'$ ; sous $F$, $G \leq F$ ; sous $X'$, $Z \overset{\circ}{\ll} X'$ (signe pointé d'un petit cercle), et $Z \ll G$ sur la dernière ligne

drawings.description: schéma (barré) : un hexagone $F, H, G$ en haut, $F', K', G'$ en bas, avec $K$ et $H'$ au centre ; flèches à crochet pour les $\leq$ ($F \to H$, $G \to H$, $K \to F$, $K \to G$, $K' \to F'$, $K' \to G'$, $F' \to H'$, $G' \to H'$) et flèches verticales pour les $\ll$ ($F' \to F$, $G' \to G$, $H' \to H$, $K' \to K$). Il est repris au propre page 74
drawings.kind: struck hexagon of inclusions F, H, G / F', K', G' with K, H' in the centre
drawings.notes: F, H, G at the top, F', K', G' at the bottom, K and H' in the centre; arrows for <= (F -> H, G -> H, K -> F, K -> G, K' -> F', K' -> G', F' -> H', G' -> H') and upward arrows for << (F' -> F, G' -> G, H' -> H, K' -> K). Hooked arrows (for <=) are drawn as plain arrows, vertical arrows (for <<) likewise; the kind of arrow is said here. Omitted as struck: the three long oblique strokes that cross out the whole diagram (it is redone fair on p. 74, drawing 04-3); the diagram under them is drawn in ink, as the transcription records it. Issue 128, 2026-11-09: struck material left out after a fresh check of the facsimile (struck-out material is not drawn). Redrawn 2026-11-09 (issue 128): to check again.

drawings.description: schéma : même disposition qu'à la page 73, au propre. En haut $H$ ; en dessous $F$ et $G$, reliés à $H$ par des flèches à crochet ; au centre $K$, relié à $F$ et à $G$ par des flèches à crochet et à $H$ par une flèche verticale, et une flèche de $K$ vers $H'$ ; puis $F'$ et $G'$, reliés à $F$ et $G$ par des flèches verticales ; en bas $K'$, relié à $F'$ et $G'$ par des flèches à crochet et à $K$ par une flèche verticale. Un premier « $F$ » en haut à gauche est biffé
drawings.kind: diagram of inclusions H; F, G; K, H'; F', G'; K' (fair copy)
drawings.notes: H at the top; F and G below, joined to H by <= arrows; K in the centre joined to F and G by <= arrows and to H by an upward arrow, and an arrow from K to H'; F' and G' joined to F and G by upward arrows; K' at the bottom joined to F' and G' by <= arrows and to K by an upward arrow. Two short strokes near F' and between H' and G' are drawn as on the page. Hooked arrows (for <=) are drawn as plain arrows, vertical arrows (for <<) likewise; the kind of arrow is said here. Omitted as struck: a first F at the top left. Issue 128, 2026-11-09: struck material left out after a fresh check of the facsimile (struck-out material is not drawn). Redrawn 2026-11-09 (issue 128): to check again.

drawings.description: schéma : un cube tronqué, de haut en bas : $H$ ; $F$ et $G$ ; $K$ et $H'$ au centre ; $H'_F$ et $H'_G$ ; $F'$, $H'_K$, $G'$ ; $F'_K$ et $G'_K$ ; $K'$. Flèches à crochet ($\leq$) : $F \to H$, $G \to H$, $K \to F$, $K \to G$, $F' \to H'_F$, $G' \to H'_G$, $H'_F \to H'$, $H'_G \to H'$, $H'_K \to H'_F$, $H'_K \to H'_G$, $F'_K \to F'$, $F'_K \to H'_K$, $G'_K \to H'_K$, $G'_K \to G'$, $K' \to F'_K$, $K' \to G'_K$ ; flèches verticales ($\ll$) : $H' \to H$, $H'_F \to F$, $H'_G \to G$, $H'_K \to K$
drawings.notes: From top to bottom: H; F and G; K and H' in the centre; H'_F and H'_G; F', H'_K, G'; F'_K and G'_K; K'. Arrows for <= : F -> H, G -> H, K -> F, K -> G, F' -> H'_F, G' -> H'_G, H'_F -> H', H'_G -> H', H'_K -> H'_F, H'_K -> H'_G, F'_K -> F', F'_K -> H'_K, G'_K -> H'_K, G'_K -> G', K' -> F'_K, K' -> G'_K; upward arrows for <<: H' -> H, H'_F -> F, H'_G -> G, H'_K -> K. Hooked arrows (for <=) are drawn as plain arrows, vertical arrows (for <<) likewise; the kind of arrow is said here.

drawings.description: schéma : $X \supseteq Y$ sur la première ligne ; sous $X$, $X' \overset{\circ}{\ll} X$ ; sous $Y$, $X'_Y \ll Y$ ; à droite, $Y' \overset{\circ}{\ll} Y$ ; sur la ligne du bas $X' \supseteq X'_Y$, avec $X'_Y = X'|Y$

drawings.description: schéma d'implications : doubles flèches de At $9_{\Sigma}$ vers At 9 et vers At 12, de At 12 vers At 10 et vers « At 11' pour $\widetilde{F}$ fini », de At 11 vers At 11', de « At 11 pour $F = \operatorname{Sup} F_i$ quelc. » vers « At 11 pour $F = \operatorname{Sup} F_i$ fini », et de At 11' vers « At 11' pour $\widetilde{F}$ fini ». Une équivalence avec « At 11 » à la fin de la dernière ligne est biffée, ainsi qu'un signe dans la marge gauche
drawings.kind: diagram of implications between axioms At 9 ... At 12
drawings.notes: Double arrows (drawn single): At 9_Sigma => At 9 and => At 12 (downwards); At 12 => At 10 and, by a bent arrow, => "At 11' pour F~ fini"; At 11 => At 11'; At 11 <=> "At 11 pour F = Sup F_i quelc.", which => "At 11 pour F = Sup F_i fini"; At 11' <=> "At 11 pour F = Sup F_i fini" (overinked, not struck: the transcription's array reads this equivalence, so it is now drawn in ink); At 11' => "At 11' pour F~ fini". Omitted as struck: the equivalence "<=> At 11" at the end of the last line and the sign in the left margin. Issue 128, 2026-11-09: struck material left out after a fresh check of the facsimile (struck-out material is not drawn). Redrawn 2026-11-09 (issue 128): to check again. Question settled by a machine pass on the facsimile, 2026-11-12 (page): the double arrow between At 11' and « At 11 pour F = Sup F_i fini » is gone over heavily along its own length, with both heads clean and no stroke across it, unlike the equivalence at the end of the last line, which is slashed and scribbled over; it is not struck and stays drawn. Not checked by a reader.

drawings.description: schéma d'implications : de « At $9_{\Sigma}$ $+$ At 10 » partent deux doubles flèches, vers At $9_{\Sigma}$ et vers At 12 ; de At $9_{\Sigma}$ une double flèche vers At 9 (critère de disj.\ par les lieux) ; de At 12 deux doubles flèches, vers At 10 et vers At 11' ; de At 11 une double flèche vers At 11'. Les légendes sont transcrites ci-dessous
drawings.kind: diagram of implications from At 9_Sigma + At 10
drawings.notes: From "At 9_Sigma + At 10" two double arrows (drawn single), to At 9_Sigma and to At 12; At 9_Sigma => At 9 (critere de disj. par les lieux); At 12 => At 10 and => At 11'; At 11 => At 11'. The captions on the right (recollement des raffinements ...) are given in short as on the page.

drawings.description: en marge gauche, devant « de ce type » : un petit ovale, repassé à droite, avec au centre un gros point précédé d'un petit signe en forme de chevron — le disque à point marqué.
drawings.notes: A small oval in the left margin, at the head of the line « de ce type », its right side gone over a second time (drawn as a second arc inside the first); at the centre a heavy point, and just left of it a small chevron-shaped sign (a pen start, or a second, open point: not read as a letter). The transcription's note says « un petit cercle contenant un signe »; on the page the sign is a heavy point with this small chevron before it. Nothing struck. Redrawn 2026-11-10 (issue 128): to check again. Question settled by a machine pass on the facsimile, 2026-11-12 (maths): the text names the figure, « disque avec pt marqué »: the heavy point is the one marked point, and the small chevron before it is not a second point; it is kept as the small stroke it is on the page. Not checked by a reader.

drawings.description: dans la ligne, à la place de « [triangle] » : un petit triangle, précédé d'un « ! », un gros point sur son côté gauche, vers le milieu.
drawings.kind: triangle with a marked point on one side
drawings.notes: A small triangle drawn in the line, a heavy point on its left side (computed on the side, at 0.6 of it from the lower left vertex), and the « ! » written just before it, left of that side. On the page the left side overshoots the lower left vertex slightly; the three sides are drawn meeting at the vertices. Nothing struck. Redrawn 2026-11-10 (issue 128): to check again. Question settled by a machine pass on the facsimile, 2026-11-12 (page): the heavy point sits on the left side of the triangle, about its middle, well away from the three vertices, as drawn. Not checked by a reader.
drawings.disagreement: The transcription's note says « un point marqué près d'un sommet »: on the page the point sits on the left side, about its middle (nearer the top vertex than the lower left one), not at a vertex.

drawings.description: à la fin de la parenthèse, après « par exemple : » : un petit cercle, repassé à droite, portant deux petites marques, l'une en haut, l'autre en bas.
drawings.notes: A small circle closing the parenthesis, after « par exemple : », its right half gone over heavily; two marks on it, placed at the top and the bottom points of the circle: at the top a small loop (drawn as an open point), at the bottom a heavy dot where the stroke seems to break and start again (drawn as a full point). Partial: whether these are two marked points (a circle cut into two arcs by two vertices) or only the start and the join of the pen stroke is not decided; the transcription sets a plain circle and its note says only « un petit cercle dessiné ». The closing parenthesis after it is text, not drawn. Redrawn 2026-11-10 (issue 128): to check again. Question settled by a machine pass on the facsimile, 2026-11-12 (page): the circle is made of two strokes, a left arc and a right arc, which meet at the two marks, at the top and at the bottom; a circle drawn in one stroke would have one start and join, not two opposite ones. The two marks are two points cutting the circle into two arcs, which is also what an example in the passage on simplicial « ateliers » calls for (two edges with the same two ends); they stay drawn. Not checked by a reader.
